slides.0.title: Grapes and styles
slides.0.subtitle: Red and rosé do the work, Muscat is the signature
slides.1.title: Red grapes
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Southern French traditions
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Carignan, Cinsault, Grenache, Mourvèdre and Alicante Bouschet, almost the same line-up as France's Mediterranean coast
slides.1.highlights.1.title: The historic workhorses
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Under the protectorate Carignan and Alicante led, followed by Grenache. The wine was mostly used for blending with wine in France
slides.1.highlights.2.title: International varieties
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Syrah, Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon are now common in premium wines, often blended with Carignan
slides.1.content: Carignan with Syrah is a good shorthand for modern Tunisian red.
slides.2.title: White grapes and Muscat
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Muscat of Alexandria
slides.2.highlights.0.content: The single variety of Kélibia, known locally as "muscat de Kélibia". Secondary sources usually describe the local Muscat as dry and fruity
slides.2.highlights.1.title: One name, two products
slides.2.highlights.1.content: In the international register, the products of Kélibia and Muscat de Thibar are "Muscat wine and Muscat mistelle". A mistelle is made by adding alcohol to unfermented grape must
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Other white grapes
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Chardonnay, Pedro Ximénez and Ugni Blanc, among others. White is a small share of output
slides.2.content: Kélibia's Muscat is Tunisia's most recognisable wine.
slides.3.title: A rosé country
slides.3.highlights.0.title: The production mix
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Figures from the Oxford Companion to Wine, 3rd edition (2006): rosé about 60–70%, red 25–30% and white under 10%. These are early-2000s shares
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Colours in the register
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Coteaux de Tébourba and Sidi Salem are registered for red and rosé only. Mornag is registered for red, rosé and white
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Grape rules
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Each region's grapes and proportions are set in its own order. This course could not read those texts, so it does not teach permitted grapes by region
slides.3.content: Red and rosé dominate, and Muscat is the white that matters.
